title: Near-best common rate mixtures give a 30-year step-response range of 0.20 to 0.41 in 54 fixed network summaries
abstract: We bound the response at a fixed time across near-best positive rate mixtures fitted to 54 published network summaries. We use 40 published annual rates and a zero-response column, with common weights and fixed spatial slopes. At a weighted fit-score allowance of 4, sharp step-response bounds are 0.177 to 0.338 after 10 years, 0.195 to 0.413 after 30 years, and 0.195 to 0.681 after 100 years, as fractions of the spatial prediction. The response at equilibrium can range from 0.195 to 1.000. At least 0.550 of the amplitude must have a half-life above 30 years or be absent. Mathematical certificates and attainable model weights verify the bounds. The below-half 30-year result holds in every leave-one-network-out fit, but fails in 46 of 200 network bootstrap draws. These are conditional sensitivity bounds, not confidence limits or forecasts. Untested rates, network differences, spatial-slope uncertainty and detection effects remain outside the analysis. Code, input hashes and aggregate results are included.

display.caption: Conditional step-response bounds across all tested near-best mixtures. The score allowance has no confidence level. Orange lines show network bootstrap endpoint percentiles. A step starts from equilibrium, not from an observed community state.

We extend the mixed-rate identification result to sharp bounds at fixed horizons; retrieval code is adapted from its MIT code.
